text:
**My pick: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W)**, which is the best all-rounder for a laptop plus a phone.

- It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A. One device gets the full 65W. Laptop plus phone on the two USB-C ports gives a 45W + 20W split, which is enough for a phone's fast charging and a MacBook Air or XPS 13 class laptop ([Anker spec page](https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY)).
- Size is about 1.5 × 1.15 × 2.6 in, with a foldable plug and GaN II. It has an 18-month warranty.
- It's $29.99 at Newegg, which Newegg lists as the #1 best seller in its category: [Buy Anker 735 at Newegg](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3).
- Cables aren't included. If all three ports are in use, power drops to 40W / 12W / 12W.

**Other good options**

- **Baseus Enercore 67W (CJ11), best tested 65W-class charger.** Tom's Hardware named it best midrange. It held full wattage through testing, ran the coolest of the group, and costs $29.99. It has a built-in retractable USB-C cable plus two more USB-C ports, so you don't need a separate cable. See the [Tom's Hardware review](https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers) for purchase links.
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W, best for travel.** Smart Gadget Kit's top pick. It weighs 113g, has three ports, and ships with US, UK and EU plug heads. Independent testing showed a 45W + 20W split with two devices connected. The USB-A port maxes out at 22.5W. See the [Smart Gadget Kit review](https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/).

**Things to know**

- 65W is shared across ports, so a laptop and phone together won't both get full speed.
- If you want Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0 (PPS), the Anker 735 spec lists PPS support. One review site says the 3-port Anker lacks it, but Anker's own page lists PPS, so I'd trust that.
- If you carry a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro, 65W will be slow under load, and you'd want a 100W charger instead.

Review sites mostly earn affiliate commissions, and the Laptopbee figures disagree with Anker's published specs in places, so I relied on Anker's specs and Tom's Hardware's testing.
